answer: Sybil resistance can come from a unique sequential work proof bound to each identity: before transacting, an agent must complete a verifiable delay computation seeded by its own public key, which cannot be parallelised or outsourced. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must therefore pay a thousand sequential time costs, while a real agent pays one. Like a delta deepening only one channel at a time, or a traveller crossing each knoll on foot, cost scales linearly with identities. A lagoon of idle copies gains nothing, as each copy still owes its own delay.
